titulo: Observability: traces and cost per cycle
lead: A loop that runs on its own must leave a trace: how long each cycle took, how many tokens it spent, what it decided and why. Without it, an error loop or a cycle that blows your quota only shows up at month's end. In this lesson you record one line per cycle and use it to get cost per cycle, cost per keep, and the alerts.
objetivo: record a trace per cycle (time, tokens, verdict) and use it to get cost per cycle, cost per keep, and the meta-agent's alerts.

aprende.t: One JSON line per cycle: the minimum worth keeping
Cost per cycle and cost per keep
Alerts: ceiling, cycles without a keep, repeated identical errors
Real tokens from a Claude Code call

hero_alt: A panel with several analog gauges and a continuous paper recorder drawing lines, with a needle with a yellow tip.

secoes.titulo: From the cycle to the alert
secoes.sub: The same role as the LOOP-R Meta-agent: it watches the system, not the problem, and only reports. Click each block.

nos.detalhe: With RASTRO=arquivo.jsonl, each cycle writes one line when it finishes, whether it's a keep, discard, or error.
cycle, description, seconds, input and output tokens (if the agent reports them), status, and reason. Names and numbers, never the text of the request or the response.
Total tokens divided by the keeps: how much one improvement that stuck costs. It is the Meta-agent's "cost per promoted hypothesis."
A cycle above 80% of the ceiling; N cycles in a row without a keep (the LOOP-R example uses 5); N errors in a row with the same reason (error loop: session limit, credential, broken tool).

secoes.legenda: The alert does not stop the loop: what stops it is the course 2 ceiling (loop-longrun.sh) or the person. Here, it is reading the trace.
secoes.dica: A trace without tokens is still useful: time, status, and reason already show an error loop and stagnation.

secoes.sub: Fake agents with made-up tokens: one expensive cycle and three identical failures (like an agent with no response because of the session limit).

blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/loop-r-eng-aprende-v72/kit
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-aprende/a7; rm -rf $E; mkdir -p $E
bash $K/novo-sistema.sh $E/sis > /dev/null; export RASTRO=$E/rastros.jsonl
c() { TOKENS_FALSOS="$2" AGENTE="bash $K/agente-falso.sh $1" bash $K/experimento.sh $E/sis "$1" > /dev/null; }
c comenta "8000 500"; c sinonimos "9000 700"; c estraga "41000 3000"   # made-up tokens for the rehearsal
c falha "0 0"; c falha "0 0"; c falha "0 0"
echo "## uma linha do rastro"; sed -n 2p $RASTRO
echo "## custo por ciclo"; python3 $K/custo-ciclo.py $RASTRO --teto 50000; echo "saída: $?"

The tokens in this rehearsal are made up (the TOKENS_FALSOS variable); time, status, and alerts come from the real script. The error loop is the case that costs the most without showing up: in course 1, the real judge stopped at the session limit from the 16th call on.

secoes.titulo: The tokens of a real call
secoes.sub: agente-claude.sh asks claude -p --output-format json and writes to the trace the sum of input (with cache) and output. One call through your subscription.

blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/loop-r-eng-aprende-v72/kit
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-aprende/a7      # the rehearsal above
RASTRO=$E/rastros.jsonl AGENTE="bash $K/agente-claude.sh" bash $K/experimento.sh $E/sis "claude"; echo "saída: $?"
tail -1 $E/rastros.jsonl | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print("tokens:", "sim" if (d["tokens_entrada"] or 0) > 0 else "não", "·", d["status"])'

abas.html:
ciclo 7 · keep · 0.800 → 1.000 · melhorou
saída: 0
tokens: sim · keep

The line written to the trace in this run: 10 seconds, 247,492 input tokens (adding cache reads and writes) and 364 output tokens. The request is under 2 KB: almost all of the input is the context that the Claude Code session loads on this machine. One measurement, Claude Code 2.1.303; yours changes with your instructions, plugins, and MCPs.

Estimating the loop's cost from the size of the request. The calculation that counts is the trace's, per cycle, with the entire context the tool loads. Cache and resume cost are covered in course 2, lesson 4.

secoes.titulo: What is already measured at INEMA
secoes.sub: Two local cases, with the date of each number.

texto: Each cycle of vendas-whatsapp has one custo.md per agent. The four cycles add up to about 1.7 million tokens for one promotion (the example's README).
Synthetic sales data, real agents: the cost is real, the effect was designed.

Claude Code hooks write events to a local SQLite (session, tool, error, subagent) and a dashboard shows what is running. Measured: 3 to 5 thousand tool calls per day, about 10 thousand events and 2 MB per day.
The project's golden rule: store names and numbers, never the text of a prompt, response, or command.
There are OpenTelemetry conventions for agents (agent spans, model-call spans, and tool spans, with tokens), described as experimental in secondary sources.
Before adopting, check the status in the OpenTelemetry documentation. One JSON line per cycle already covers what this lesson asks for.

exercicios.pronto: ALERTA: ciclo 3 usou 88% do teto, ALERTA: 3 erros seguidos iguais, and saída: 1.

exercicios.texto: Run the real block right after the rehearsal.
exercicios.pronto: the last printed line starts with tokens: sim; if it comes out as tokens: não · erro, the agent got no response (session limit): wait and run again.

exercicios.texto: Hook RASTRO into your experiment (or write the same JSON line at the end of each cycle of your loop) and set the per-cycle token ceiling from the real measurement in E20.
exercicios.pronto: python3 $K/custo-ciclo.py [your trace] --teto [your ceiling] lists one cycle per line and ends in sem alerta or in an ALERTA: that you can explain.

perguntas.p: Six cycles, one keep, 62,200 tokens in total. What is the cost per keep?
perguntas.explica: Total divided by the keeps: 62,200 / 1. The cost per keep includes the attempts that didn't stay.

perguntas.p: Three cycles in a row end in an error with the same reason. What is this usually?
opcoes: An error loop: session limit, credential, or broken tool
A sign the loop has converged and there is nothing left to improve in the system
perguntas.explica: A bad hypothesis gives a discard, not an error. The same repeated error is infrastructure, and every round costs time and quota.

opcoes: Names and numbers: cycle, time, tokens, status, reason
The full text of the request and the response, so you can reproduce the cycle later
perguntas.explica: Numbers are enough for cost and alerts, and prompt and response text may hold sensitive data. This is the INEMA local telemetry rule.

perguntas.p: In the real call that was measured, the request was under 2 KB and the input went over 247 thousand tokens. Why?
opcoes: The trace added up the previous ten calls by mistake
The session carries a lot of context beyond the request
perguntas.explica: Instructions, memory, and the rest of the harness go into every call. That is why you measure cost in the trace, not in the size of the request.

itens.texto: Each cycle records time, tokens, status, and reason; no prompt text.
Total tokens over the improvements that stayed; it includes the attempts that didn't stay.
Ceiling, cycles without a keep, and repeated errors in a row; the alert reports, and the ceiling and the person stop.
